title: Refine continuous-batching thresholds & KV-cache eviction to prevent GPU memory blowouts under sustained high QPS
creator: Priya Patel
description: Production clusters have seen repeated GPU OOMs and long tail latency spikes when sustained QPS exceeds 10k per region. Root cause analysis points to (1) continuous micro-batching growing beyond safe thresholds under bursty arrivals, (2) unbounded KV cache population holding large embedding KV blobs in GPU memory, and (3) lack of a coordinated backpressure signal between request admission and per-GPU batch builders. This ticket scopes an engineering workstream to (A) introduce a dynamic micro-batch ceiling that adapts to free GPU memory and recent latency SLO violations, (B) implement size-aware KV-cache eviction and eviction prefetching to keep a reserved memory budget for active requests, and (C) add a front-door backpressure mechanism that enforces an in-flight request cap and graceful degradation path when memory pressure is high.
acceptance_criteria: No CUDA OOMs observed in canary cluster under sustained 20k QPS for 30 minutes (simulated workload with real seq length distribution)
99th percentile generation latency <= 250ms on the canary workload while maintaining >=90% of baseline throughput
KV cache stays within configured GPU reservation (default 60%) across sustained workloads; eviction logs show size-aware evictions and no sudden memory spikes
Backpressure signal reduces accepted QPS by at least 25% before any OOMs and exposes a clear metric on the console (per-GPU in-flight and memory headroom)
Automated unit + integration tests exercising dynamic ceiling adjustments, eviction policy, and backpressure behaviors included in CI
tasks: Instrument current batcher to expose per-GPU free memory and live in-flight request counts
Design dynamic ceiling algorithm: combine EWMA of allocation rate, absolute free bytes floor, and latency SLO feedback
Implement size-aware KV cache eviction (eviction candidates ranked by memory footprint and last access)
Add a memory reservation region for active batches so KV cache cannot consume critical allocation slots
Implement front-door token-bucket backpressure controller that integrates with routing layer and emits throttle events
Create e2e load test harness simulating production seq-length distribution and mixed short+long generations
Add Grafana dashboards and console widgets: per-GPU headroom, microbatch ceiling, eviction rate, throttle rate
Ship canary rollout with automatic rollback on OOMs and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets
decisions: Use conservative default reservation of 40% GPU memory for in-flight work and 60% for cache (configurable per-cluster)
Eviction strategy: size-aware LRU variant (entries ranked by last access time * size) to prefer removing large low-reuse entries
Dynamic ceiling recalculation interval set to 250ms to balance responsiveness and stability
Backpressure mechanism will be applied at the routing layer with a soft-throttle (reject-with-429) plus optional queueing in Dedicated mode
No immediate change to model kernels or quantization in this ticket — focus is on admission and cache management
tradeoffs: Reserving GPU memory for in-flight work reduces effective cache capacity and may increase cache miss rate; mitigated by smarter eviction and prefetching
Shorter recalculation interval improves responsiveness to sudden spikes but can cause oscillation in microbatch sizes; chosen 250ms as compromise
Soft 429 throttles provide clearer operational signal but can impact customer latency/availability; will gate behavior behind tiered flags for Hosted vs Dedicated
Size-aware eviction increases CPU overhead for eviction decisions — acceptable given reduced OOM incidents and fewer expensive restarts
